## From Hourly to Annual: Your 38-Hour Week, Fortnight, and Year

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, it helps to see the full picture: what you'll earn in a year, a fortnight, and after tax and super. This guide uses a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year, the most common full-time assumption in Australia. We'll also touch on how **salary packaging not for profit australia** can change your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours, that's hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. A fortnight's gross pay would be the weekly amount (hourly × 38) multiplied by 2.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. This is the floor for award-free employees. Many workers are covered by awards, which have higher minimum rates set by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate—so a casual on the minimum wage earns $33.05 per hour. This calculator lets you check a box to add casual loading; never enter a rate that already includes it.

### Tax and Medicare in 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office's resident tax rates for 2026–27 are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. This calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). It does not deduct HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $80,000 salary, super would be $9,600 per year. This calculator estimates super separately from your gross pay.

### Salary Packaging Not for Profit Australia

If you work for a not-for-profit organisation, you may be able to salary package certain benefits (like a car or living expenses) using pre-tax income. This reduces your taxable income and can increase your take-home pay. However, this calculator does not model salary packaging. For a more accurate estimate, use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base rate, then consider how packaging might affect your tax. You can also read more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Using the Calculator

Start at [the timesheet](/). Type your base hourly rate. If you're casual, check the box to add 25% loading. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember: it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It's an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For a full-time worker on $30 per hour, that's $30 × 38 = $1,140 per week, or $2,280 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay will be lower. Use the calculator to see your estimated net pay each fortnight.

### Average Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.7 per week. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.2 per week. These are averages, not medians for your job. Your own rate may differ based on your award, industry, and experience.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52. For full-time, that's hourly × 38 × 52.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour; casual rate is $33.05.
- Super is 12% on top, up to the $270,830 cap.
- Tax brackets and Medicare apply; salary packaging not for profit australia can reduce taxable income.
- This calculator is a starting point. For exact figures, consult a tax professional or your employer.
